scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements for materials, manufacture, dimensions, tolerances, and testing parameters for structural plywood intended for use in load-bearing applications such as flooring, roofing, beams, joists, and structural walling panels. It is designed to sustain static and dynamic mechanical loads under varying atmospheric moisture exposure.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Plywood and Wooden Flush Door Shutters (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Structural Plywood manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, stocking, or selling uncertified structural-grade plywood in the domestic market is a criminal offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. MSMEs are granted specific phased transition periods, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to wood panels.

requirements.detail: Every structural plywood panel must be legibly and indelibly marked on its face or edge with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's name or trademark, grade, thickness, type, and licence number (CM/L).

Veneers must be peeled from timbers of specified hardwood species (Annex B) with high natural durability. Only BWP-grade synthetic resin adhesives conforming to IS 848 must be used to ensure water-proof covalent bonding.

Plywood is classified into three structural types based on composition: a) Type 1 (CS): Structural Plywood with core and face veneers of the same species; b) Type 2 (CSC): Structural Plywood with core of one species and face veneers of other species; c) Type 3 (CSFF): Structural Plywood Film Faced (phenolic film-faced).
Core and face veneers must undergo deep chemical vacuum-pressure impregnation (typically CCB or copper naphthenate) to ensure the entire panel is 100% borer, fungus, and termite proof.
Finished structural plywood boards must be seasoned to maintain a uniform moisture content within the range of 5 to 15 percent when tested per IS 1734 (Part 1).
When tested in the dry state per IS 1734 (Part 4), the panel must develop high adhesion strength: a) Average failing load: minimum 1350 N; b) Minimum individual failing load: minimum 1100 N.

After 72 hours of continuous boiling water immersion (to simulate extreme weather stress), the panel must satisfy: a) Average failing load: minimum 1000 N; b) Minimum individual failing load: minimum 800 N; c) Adhesion of plies (Knife Test): Pass.
The panel must resist fungal attacks. After mycological conditioning, the glue lines must satisfy: a) Average failing load: minimum 1000 N; b) Minimum individual failing load: minimum 800 N.

Along the face grain (parallel), the structural plywood must develop high load-bearing capacity: a) Modulus of Rupture (MOR): Average minimum 50 N/mm² (MPa), Minimum individual 45 N/mm²; b) Modulus of Elasticity (MOE): Average minimum 7500 N/mm² (MPa), Minimum individual 6700 N/mm².

Across the face grain (perpendicular), the structural plywood must meet: a) Modulus of Rupture (MOR): Average minimum 30 N/mm² (MPa), Minimum individual 27 N/mm²; b) Modulus of Elasticity (MOE): Average minimum 4000 N/mm², Minimum individual 3600 N/mm².
The structural panel must offer exceptional grip: a) Screw holding strength: minimum 1600 N; b) Nail holding strength: minimum 1300 N.

All boards of the identical thickness and size dispatched against one dispatch note constitute a lot. Random samples must be selected as per Table 3 to perform visual, dimensional, and physical-mechanical testing.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10701 : 2012 is the mandatory national Indian Standard safety specification regulating Structural Grade Plywood used in high-load, structural, and infrastructure construction applications (such as flooring, roofing, beams, joists, and structural walling). Under India's statutory Plywood Quality Control Order (QCO), all structural plywood sold or imported in India must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to ensure safety and prevent structural failures. Unlike ordinary plywood grades, IS 10701 focuses heavily on structural mechanical performance—enforcing strict minimum limits on Modulus of Rupture (MOR ≥ 50 MPa along the grain) and Modulus of Elasticity (MOE ≥ 7500 MPa along the grain) to minimize deflection under heavy loads. It mandates the use of hardwood veneers bonded with unextended Boiling Water Proof (BWP) phenolic resins, vacuum-pressure preservative treatments to render the boards 100% termite and borer proof, and a 5-15% moisture content to prevent warping or delamination.
